prompt: We're planning to move the TicketBooking service from single-region to active-active across us-east-1 and us-west-2. The design document is in docs/design/active-active-regions.md, with supporting context in the docs and data folders. I need you to review this design before we commit to implementation. We've had past issues with regional outages causing revenue loss, so availability and data consistency are critical. Look for gaps in the approach, contradictions with our service targets, and risks we might have missed. Write your review to REVIEW.md at the top of the project. End the review with a fenced json list of findings, each with location (the section number of the document, like 3.2), severity (critical, high, medium, low or nit), issue and fix. Focus on concrete problems that would affect users or the business if we built it as designed.

checks.cmd: node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const t=fs.readFileSync("REVIEW.md","utf8");let L=null;for(const m of t.matchAll(/^\x60\x60\x60([a-z]*)[ \t]*\n([\s\S]*?)^\x60\x60\x60[ \t]*$/gim)){if(m[1]&&m[1].toLowerCase()!=="json")continue;let d;try{d=JSON.parse(m[2])}catch{continue}const l=Array.isArray(d)?d:Array.isArray(d&&d.findings)?d.findings:null;if(l&&l.every(x=>x&&typeof x==="object"&&!Array.isArray(x))){L=l;break}}if(!L||!L.length)process.exit(1);const S=["critical","high","medium","low","nit"];process.exit(L.every(x=>x.location&&S.includes(String(x.severity).toLowerCase())&&(x.issue||x.fix||x.text))?0:1)'

node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const t=fs.readFileSync("REVIEW.md","utf8");let L=null;for(const m of t.matchAll(/^\x60\x60\x60([a-z]*)[ \t]*\n([\s\S]*?)^\x60\x60\x60[ \t]*$/gim)){if(m[1]&&m[1].toLowerCase()!=="json")continue;let d;try{d=JSON.parse(m[2])}catch{continue}const l=Array.isArray(d)?d:Array.isArray(d&&d.findings)?d.findings:null;if(l&&l.every(x=>x&&typeof x==="object"&&!Array.isArray(x))){L=l;break}}if(!L||!L.length)process.exit(1);const H=new Set();for(const l of fs.readFileSync("docs/design/active-active-regions.md","utf8").split("\n")){const m=l.match(/^#+\s*(?:section\s*)?(\d+(?:\.\d+)*)/i);if(m)H.add(m[1])}process.exit(L.every(x=>{const m=String(x.location).match(/\d+(?:\.\d+)*/);return m&&H.has(m[0])})?0:1)'

rubric.criterion: Each important finding explains the concrete consequence in this project and proposes a fix a developer can act on, without inventing problems that don't exist (code cannot check this because it requires understanding the business context and technical tradeoffs)

findingsKey.finding: Last-write-wins conflict resolution allows the same seat to be sold in both regions, violating the core business rule against double booking.
The claimed RPO of 60 seconds in section 6.3 is smaller than the measured replication lag which exceeds 60 seconds at P99, meaning data loss could exceed the recovery target.
DNS TTL of 300 seconds plus health check timing of 60 seconds exceeds the 60-second RTO stated in section 6.2, meaning failover will take longer than the recovery target.
The budget allocation in section 8.1 omits the doubled database cost for the second region and underestimates cross-region data transfer costs.
The failback procedure in section 7.1 is vague and missing detailed steps for verifying data consistency before returning traffic to the restored region.
A global seats-left counter updated in both regions with no merge rule will cause inventory discrepancies and potential overselling.
The estimated recovery time in section 6.1 doesn't account for DNS propagation delay beyond TTL, which could extend the actual outage duration.
Asynchronous replication contradicts the strong consistency requirement for seat inventory stated in the product rules, creating dependency compatibility issues.

items.text: Asks how the design handles partial regional failures where the database is available but dependent services like PaymentGateway or UserService are not.
Questions how the application ensures idempotency of booking operations during retries after network timeouts or partial failures.
Identifies the need for circuit breakers to prevent cascading failures when cross-region calls experience latency spikes or timeouts.
Asks about the strategy for schema migrations and maintaining backward compatibility during rolling deployments across regions.
Questions how the design handles clock skew between regions which could affect timestamp-based conflict resolution.
Identifies the need for canary deployments and feature flags to control rollouts and mitigate risk during the migration.
Asks about monitoring and alerting for data drift between regions before it causes business impact or requires manual reconciliation.
Questions how session replication handles failover when Redis clusters experience regional outages or network partitions.

weakAnswers: The design looks comprehensive and well thought out overall.
Consider adding more details about scalability for future growth.
Make sure to include proper error handling and logging throughout.
The team should think about security implications of cross-region data transfer.
Add more testing scenarios to ensure robustness.

verdicts.note: Prompt does not name a review method, checklist or process. Does not hint at planted problems or their area. Does not give the number of problems.
Clear what to review (design doc), where to write (REVIEW.md), and output format (JSON with location, severity, issue, fix). Section numbers provide unambiguous location references.

Key items require cross-referencing multiple files (design doc + CSV data + service targets + product rules). Many findings require connecting design claims to contradictory evidence. A shallow review would miss several items (especially k2 requiring CSV analysis, k1 requiring understanding of the conflict scenario, k8 requiring cross-referencing consistency requirements).

All 8 key items are verifiable: k1 (3.2 last-write-wins vs product-rules double-booking ban), k2 (6.3 RPO 60s vs CSV p99 lag 450-720ms), k3 (6.2 RTO 60s vs 3.5 DNS TTL 300s + health check timing), k4 (8.1 budget omits doubled DB cost), k5 (7.1 vague failback), k6 (3.3 no merge rule for global counter), k7 (6.1 no DNS propagation consideration), k8 (2.2 strong consistency vs 3.2 async replication). Section numbers are accurate. Severity ratings are defensible.

No comments, tests, or file names point to planted problems. The fixture presents the design neutrally. The README lists contents without hints. The dry-run dump achieves 7/20, confirming some difficulty.
